candidate_relations.reason: Calciphylaxis can produce retiform purpura and necrotic skin lesions in a similar distribution, making it a plausible differential, but the clinical context here points specifically to heparin-induced skin necrosis: recent subcutaneous heparin administration, positive antiplatelet antibody test (IgG and polyvalent), no injection-site lesion, and no typical calciphylaxis risk factors (e.g., end-stage renal disease, hyperparathyroidism, calcium-phosphate dysregulation). Calciphylaxis asserts an incompatible etiology and mechanism compared to the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Calciphylaxis is a distinct vascular calcification syndrome; the reference diagnosis is heparin-induced skin necrosis at a distant site

case_quality_flags: Positive antiplatelet antibodies (IgG and polyvalent) strongly support heparin-induced thrombocytopenia/skin necrosis mechanism rather than calciphylaxis
GFR 45.8 mL/min is consistent with CKD stage 3b but insufficient alone to support calciphylaxis without additional metabolic derangements
